name: PLG Usage-Signal Outreach (PostHog → n8n → LiteLLM → Twenty + Slack)

meta.description: A PostHog product-usage event webhook fires; n8n checks audience eligibility, computes the cumulative usage threshold via a HogQL query, applies negative conditions + cooldown/frequency caps, drafts a context-aware message via a self-hosted LiteLLM proxy, and (unless DRY_RUN) writes the lead to Twenty CRM and notifies a rep in Slack to review and send. Human-in-the-loop: no message is auto-sent to the end user. All external calls use $env credentials and placeholder-shaped requests you adapt to your instances.

nodes.name: Webhook — PostHog Event
nodes.notes: Point a PostHog "Webhook destination" (CDP -> Destinations) at this URL, filtered to the events your triggers care about. Expected body: { distinct_id, event, timestamp, properties:{ email,name,company,plan,marketing_consent, ... } }. See src/posthog-webhook.example.json.

nodes.name: Normalize Event
nodes.notes: Pass the PostHog payload through. Adjust here if your PostHog webhook wraps the body differently (see config/schema-map.yml for field mapping).

nodes.name: Query PostHog Usage (HogQL)
nodes.notes: PostHog Query API (HogQL). Placeholder: verify the endpoint + HogQL syntax for your PostHog version. Returns { results: [[trigger_count, negative_count]] }. This is where the CUMULATIVE threshold is computed (PostHog native webhooks fire per-event; the aggregate is evaluated here, as the source describes: the threshold rule is glue in the orchestrator).

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, action: 'no-send', reason: $json.reason, triggerCount: $json.triggerCount }) }}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'outreach-drafter', max_tokens: 300, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: $json.llm.system }, { role: 'user', content: $json.llm.user } ] }) }}

nodes.name: Compose Message (LiteLLM)
nodes.notes: Self-hosted LiteLLM proxy, OpenAI-compatible. Returns choices[0].message.content = the drafted message. Even in DRY_RUN this runs (small token cost) so the preview shows the REAL draft; the offline harness in src/ uses a deterministic stand-in instead.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, action: 'dry-run-preview', trigger: $('Build Prompt').item.json.trigger.id, contact: { name: $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.name, email: $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.email, company: $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.company }, draft: ($json.choices && $json.choices[0] && $json.choices[0].message && $json.choices[0].message.content) || '(no draft returned)', note: 'DRY_RUN=true: no CRM write, no Slack notify, no send recorded.' }) }}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'mutation Create($data: PersonCreateInput!) { createPerson(data: $data) { id } }', variables: { data: { emails: { primaryEmail: $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.email }, name: { firstName: $('Build Prompt').item.json.firstName, lastName: '' }, jobTitle: 'PLG signal: ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.trigger.id } } }) }}

nodes.name: Create CRM Record (Twenty)
nodes.notes: Twenty GraphQL. PLACEHOLDER mutation - adapt to your workspace schema (custom fields, dedupe/upsert, and a linked Note object carrying the drafted message + signal). Twenty auto-generates both REST (/rest) and GraphQL (/graphql) CRUD; see docs.twenty.com. For real use, resolve-or-create the person (query by email first) rather than blind create.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $env.SLACK_CHANNEL_ID, text: 'PLG signal: ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.trigger.id + ' — ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.company, blocks: [ { type: 'section', text: { type: 'mrkdwn', text: '*Product-usage signal:* ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.trigger.id + '
*User:* ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.name + ' <' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.email + '> (' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.company + ')
*Signal:* ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.trigger.event + ' reached ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.triggerCount + ' in ' + $('Build Prompt').item.json.trigger.window } }, { type: 'section', text: { type: 'mrkdwn', text: '*Suggested draft (review before sending):*
' + (($('Compose Message (LiteLLM)').item.json.choices && $('Compose Message (LiteLLM)').item.json.choices[0].message.content) || '(no draft)') } } ] }) }}

nodes.name: Notify Slack (rep)
nodes.notes: Human-in-the-loop: this pings a REP with the drafted message to review and send. The workflow does NOT auto-send to the end user (the source stack names no email/ESP). Requires a bot token with chat:write.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, action: 'sent-to-rep', trigger: $('Build Prompt').item.json.trigger.id, contact: $('Build Prompt').item.json.person.email }) }}
